## Why This Is Asked
Tests CGO callback bridges, memory ownership, and thread-safety when Go calls into C and C calls back into Go.

## Key Concepts
- CGO callback export and cgo rules
- Memory ownership and avoiding GC lifetimes crossing boundaries
- Thread-safety with concurrent Go calls into C
- Safe passing of Go pointers via context handles

## Code Example
```c
// header
typedef void (*cb_t)(int result, void* ctx);
void sum_with_callback(const int* data, size_t n, cb_t cb, void* ctx);
```

```go
// binding sketch
//export go_cb
func go_cb(res C.int, ctx unsafe.Pointer) { /* translate to Go */ }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle panics in the Go callback?
- How do you ensure callbacks are not invoked after the Go GC moves data?
